facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: The Process start calendar is evaluated and used in the simulation algorithm "Workload Analysis". It describes the occurrences of the business processes over one year. It is possible to define a number of "typical" day profiles which can then be assigned to all the days of the year. The day profile is constructed by time intervals within which a probability distribution is assigned. Those probability distributions within the various day profiles describe the time between two process starts.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value: The possibility is offered to call other processes with the object 'Subprocess'. This is useful when a subprocess is called more than once within a model or where there is a need to structure the business process in subprocesses so that overview will be increased. Besides this it is possible to set more variables as parameters to the Subprocess.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
The value of this attribute is needed for the simulation. It is possible to assign a performer, that is, a reference between business processes and working environment. Through this it is possible to aggregate the concequenses of the performers and roles on the workload, via simulation (Capacity and Workload analysis). At the top right of the field 'Performer' you will find a dialog button which will give assistance in making performer assignments.
Apart from the static elements of AQL also the dynamic elements of 'performer of' and 'done by' can be used in the Capacity and Workload analysis.
'performer of': (process intern, syntax: performer of <Activity>) The result is the performer of the working environment model, who executed the activity during simulation. This way it is secured that an activity will be executed by the same performer as assigned in the perfomer field. Example: performer of "Contract be filed"
'done by': (process interreferenced, syntax: done by <Variable>) The result is the performer of the working environment model, who executes the activity during simulation, at which the variable refers to. To use this construction the name of the variable of the refered activity should be entered in the 'done by' attribute. Example: done by "Contract performer"

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
This is the time taken to actually execute the activity.
The format for time is yy:ddd:hh:mm:ss (years-days-hours-minutes-seconds). The deafult value for each time field is 00:000:00:00:00, i.e. the value of each time type will be zero in the simulation, if no time value is entered. The value in this field is used in the simulation algorithms

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
This is the time between the possible and the actual start of the execution of the activity.
The format for time is yy:ddd:hh:mm:ss (years-days-hours-minutes-seconds). The deafult value for each time field is 00:000:00:00:00, i.e. the value of each time type will be zero in the simulation, if no time value is entered. The value in this field is used in the simulation algorithms

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
This is the time between the completion of an activity and its transport to the following activity.
The format for time is yy:ddd:hh:mm:ss (years-days-hours-minutes-seconds). The deafult value for each time field is 00:000:00:00:00, i.e. the value of each time type will be zero in the simulation, if no time value is entered. The value in this field is used in the simulation algorithms

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: This is the time used for transport to the next activity. The format for time is yy:ddd:hh:mm:ss (years-days-hours-minutes-seconds). The deafult value for each time field is 00:000:00:00:00, i.e. the value of each time type will be zero in the simulation, if no time value is entered. The value in this field is used in the simulation algorithms

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: Enter the priority for the activity to be executed. The largest the value of this attribute, the highest the activity's priority. The execution of activity's in the simulation is done according to the priority. Activities in the same priority are worked out in delivery order.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
By entering a variable name into this attribute, the name of the performer who executes the activity will be saved into that variable. Through the 'done by' construct it is possible to refer to this variable during execution of interreference AQL expression (Capacity and Workload analysis).
Example: Assign to the 'done by' field: Application performer <Variable>) The reference to the Application performer through an AQL expression: done by "Application performer"

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: yes@no

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
Hint: The 'Continuous execution' is evaluated by the simulation algorithm 'Workload Analysis'.
If 'continuous execution' is activated (value: yes) then this means this activity will be executed by the same performer (if possible) as in the previous activity. This activity will be placed at the top of the list of orders that should be executed by the performer, so that execution by the performer is secured in order to avoid (unrealistic) waiting time.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: The maximum resource waiting time declares the resource waiting time period for which a performer awaits the neccessary resources to become available. If the resource waiting time is greater than declared, the performer will reassign the activity within the task stack, For example: If the value of this attribute is: 00:000:00:05:00. This means that the performer of this task will wait maximum 5 minutes for the neccessary resource to become available. This task will then be attempted again when the following task has been completed.

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: yes@no

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: An activity is co-operative (value: yes) when more than one performer, out of potential performers, is choosen to execute it, when the activity is delegated to all potential performers. The execution of the activity by the performers starts when enough performers are available (see 'Average number of participants' and 'Max start period'). The execution of an activity by the performers may be either synchronous which means that all performers must execute it at the same time or asynchronous where there is a time slack (see 'Cooperation mode').

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: synchron@asynchron

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: A synchronous activity (value: synchron) is executed by all performers to whom the activity has benn delegated at the same time (see 'Average number of participants' and 'Min. quota of presence'). An asynchronous executed activity (value: asynchron), is being executed by all performers with the time slack, i.e. as soon as one performer is available for the execution of the delegated activity.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: This attribute is evaluated by the simulation algorithm 'Path Analysis' during the execution of co-operative activities. During path analysis, activities are not assigned to specific performers. Therefore a co-operative activity is doubled during analysis by the 'Average number of participants' and these are then executed like parallel activities.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: This attribute is evaluated during the execution of the co-operative activities by the simulation algorithm 'Workload Analysis'. It refers to the minimum number of performers who must be present before a synchronous, co-operative activity can be executed. If a sufficient number of performers are not available, the activity is delayed until they become available. The maximum delay period is held in the attribute 'Max start period'.

domain.val-message: The minimum quota of presence needs to have a value between 0 and 100.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value: This attribute is evaluated during the execution of the co-operative activities by the simulation algorithm 'Workload Analysis'. The value of the 'Max. start period' attribute indicates the maximum length of time for which a co-operative activity may not be executed until a sufficient number of performers is available (see 'Min. quota of presence').

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: yes@no

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
Hint: This attribute is evaluated only in the Workload Analysis
When the activity is 'Execution interruptable' (Value: 'yes') then the execution of the process is interrupted at this activity when the working time of the performer is ended. When the activity is not execution interruptable the process will continue also in the performers free time

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: personal@global

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
Hint: This attribute is evaluated only in the Workload Analysis
Choose 'personal' when the activity is to be executed directly by a specific performer. The assignment will be successful even if the performer is not currently available. The activity remains in the performer's task stack until he executes it. Choose 'global' when the activity may be executed by the next free performer. Only available performers may execute activities

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
Select the type of distribution and the corresponding parameters. The syntax for entering a continious distribution is:
- for normal distribution: Normal(<Number 1>; <Number 2>) Enter the expectancy and the standard deviation for the normal distribution, where (Number1) is the expectancy and (Number2) the standard deviation. Example: Normal( 1200; 100 ) - the variable has a normal distribution with an expected value of 1200 and a standard deviation of 100.
- for exponential distribution: Exponential( <Number> ) Enter the expected value for the exponential distribution where <Number> corresponds to 1 divided by the expectancy (1/E). Example: Exponential( 0.002 ) - the value is distributed exponentially with the expectancy of 500.
- for uniform distribution: Uniform( <Number1> ; <Number2> ) Enter the boundaries for the normal distribution where <Number1> is the lower boundary and <Number2> the upper. Example: Equal( 0 ; 100 ) - the variable is distributed uniformly between the boundaries of 0 and 100.
- for discrete distribution: Discrete( <Symbol1> <Number1>; <Symbol2> <Number2> ;... ) You can define one or more symbols with their probabilities of occurrence (Number1, Number2, ... ). Note the sum of all the probabilites for a discrete distribution must be 1! Example: Discrete( YES 0.6; NO 0.4 ) - the variable is assigned with the value 'YES' with a probability of 0.6, NO with a probability of 0.4. Note the transition conditions are defined as follows <Variable name>='YES' or <Variable name>='NO'. For cycles, it is possible to assign more than one distribution to the attribute 'Value' so that the value is changed in every cycle. Separate the distribution with ';'. During simulation the first distribution will be run in the first cycle, the second distribution in the second cycle etc.

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value: A decision is used in a process model to set questions on defined variables and construct alternative process paths. Each simulation has only one predecessor. The object 'Decision' must have at least one predecessor and at least one successor. Only one path should be possible after decision during the simulation business process

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value:
Parallelity enables the system to run through several different paths in a process at the same time. Through parallelity it is possible independent process parts to be executed at the same time . Parallelity is terminated with merging. The object 'Parallelity' has at least one predecessor and at least one successor. A transition condition may also be assigned to the 'subsequent' connector in order to link independent paths with a decision. Note that the structure of more parallel paths can be achieved by intraconnection.
The object 'Parallelity' should usually have as many successors as predecessors has the corresponding object 'Merging'. The only exception is that through a decision a path is being splited in two or more (logigal) paths. The parallelity requirement is fullfilled through the fact that there is only one path after a decision. The object 'Merging' is allowed to receive only as many paths as those exiting the object 'Parallelity'.

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value: Merging reunites parallel paths into one path. The object 'Merging' has exactly as many predecessors as the related object 'Parallelity' has successors. 'Merging' has at most one successor'.

facet.name: EnumerationDomain
facet.value: local@global

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
A local end indicates the end of the current business process and the return to a calling business process. The path will then continue through the calling process.
A global end indicates the end of the current business process and the return to the calling business process. However the path in the calling process is now interrupted and returns to its calling process... and so on... until the entire process ends. If a global end occurs inside a parallelity, then the path continues until the corresponding merging and then the process ends as described above.

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value: The object 'End' indicates the end of a path of a business process. There can be many objects of the class 'End' in a model. This object has at least one predecessor and no successors.

Variables are used in models in order to define transition conditions. These transition conditions are defined in the relation 'Subsequent' (after a decision or a parallelity). The object 'Variable' has neither a predecessor nor a successor. The object 'Variable' can be linked to the following objects:
- 'Random generator' through the relation 'Sets variable' - 'Process start' through the relation 'Parameter' - 'Subprocess' through the relation 'Call parameter'
A variable can be instantiated with different values at different times by using several objects of the class 'Random generator'.

classattribute.value:
The random generator is used to assign values to variables. The variable may be assigned with a value by a normal, exponential, uniform or discrete distribution function. An object of class 'Random generator' has no predecessors and no successors'. It can be connected to the following objects:
- 'Variable' by the relation 'Sets variable' - 'Process start' and 'Activity' by the relation 'Sets'
Several Random generators may be connected to one Variable

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
The value of this attribute is used in the simulation algorithms, 'Capacity Analysis' and 'Workload Analysis'. It is possible to assign resources, i.e. to link activities with the resources that are required to execute them. The effect of resources on the cycle time and waiting time of a business process can be examined by investigating the activities which use resources . Mouse-clicking on the dialogue button above the selection box will give support on assigning resources.
In addition to the static elements of AQL, it is possible to use the dynamic construct 'current Performer' for ressource assignment. (Syntax: current Performer -> <Ressource relation> It guarantees that the particular performer will use during the execution of the activity the assigned ressources.

classattribute.name: HlpTxt
classattribute.value: Resources are evaluated in the simulation algorithms 'Volume Analysis' and 'Workload Analysis'. An object of the class resource within a business process model represents exactly one object of the class resource in a working environment model. The assignment is succeded by an AQL expression, which is dynamically considered during the simulation. During the execution of one simulation, a resource from the working environment model is assigned to a resource in the business process model the first time it is used. For the rest of this particular simulation, the same resource will be used.

facet.name: AttributeHelpText
facet.value:
A transition condition consists either of one elementary expression or several elementary expressions which are linked together by OR, AND or NOT. The linking is succeeded with the expression NOT, OR or AND.
Examples: (a) (<elementary expression1>) AND (<elementary expression2>) (b) (<elementary expression1>) AND (<elementary expression2>) (c) NOT (<elementary expression1>) (d) (<elementary expression1>) AND (NOT (<elementary expression2>))
An elementary expression is defined as: <Variable name><Operator><Constant> where - <Variable name> - the name of an instantiated variable, - <Operator> - may be <, > or = - <Constant> - a numeric or alphanumeric expression (a numeric expression may only consist of integers; an alphanumeric expression must be delimited by single quotes). For example: (a) X='Yes' - this condition is fulfilled if the variable X has the value 'Yes' (X is assigned values through a discrete distribution!) (b) (X='Yes') AND (Y='Yes'), this condition is fulfilled where variables X and Y have the value 'Yes' (X dnd Y are discrete distributed!) (c) Z<1000, this condition is fulfilled if Z is less than 1000 (Z is continually distributed!) (d) NOT(Z<1000), this condition is fulfilled if Z greater or equal 1000 is (complementary to Z<1000, Z is continually distributed!) (e) (X='NO') OR (NOT (Z=1000)), this condition is fulfilled if either X has the value 'NO' or Z is not equal to 1000 (X is discrete, Z is continually distributed!)
